case_title: Sahib Hussain @ Sahib Jan v. State of Rajasthan
accused_victim_relationship: Prior dispute: quarrel with deceased Seema on the day of Eid
evidence_type: Circumstantial evidence, including extra-judicial confession, recoveries, medical (post-mortem) evidence, motive, and conduct; no eyewitness
confession: Extra-judicial confession made by the accused to PW-4 (a friend); relied on along with other material evidence
aggravating_circumstances: Five deaths including three children; multiple injuries on the bodies
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.302; sentenced to death
high_court_outcome: Appeals dismissed; conviction upheld; death sentence commuted to life imprisonment with at least 20 years before release and no remission
offence_finally_established: Murder under IPC s.302 (deaths of five persons)
neutral_facts: On the night of 27 October 2006, at about 10.30 p.m., a resident of the same colony, while walking home, found the accused talking to another resident and heard him say that he had killed a woman, three children and a man. The witness went to the house and found the man lying in a pool of blood outside a room, and the bodies of a young man, the woman and two children inside the rooms. He informed the household's employer by telephone, and a written report was given to police. The man was taken to hospital but died on the way. Post-mortem reports recorded multiple injuries to the bodies, and medical evidence showed all five deaths were homicidal. No eyewitness saw the killings. The second resident said the accused had told him about the incident and that he had changed his clothes and run towards the highway. The accused was said to have had a quarrel with the woman on the day of a festival. After the incident the accused allegedly left the village and boarded a bus to another city. Police stopped the bus, and the accused first gave a false name before giving his true name. On the accused's disclosure statement, a blood-stained axe, clothes and blood-stained chappals were recovered in the presence of two witnesses. Forensic and DNA reports matched blood groups on the chappals, trousers, shirt and axe with those of the deceased.
physical_harm: Death of five persons (Seema, Munna Mawali, Kalu, Isha and Sonu) from multiple injuries
motive: Alleged: quarrel with deceased Seema on the day of Eid; court said the corroborated incident cannot be ruled out
key_evidence_accepted: Testimony of PW-1 and PW-4; extra-judicial confession to PW-4; recoveries of axe, clothes and chappals (PW-2, PW-3); FSL and DNA reports; post-mortem and medical evidence; conduct and false name at arrest
witness_credibility: PW-1 and PW-4 found acceptable with no valid reason to disbelieve; PW-4 found reliable and inspiring confidence; PW-2 and PW-3 recoveries found acceptable
post_offence_conduct: Left village immediately after incident and boarded bus to Delhi; arrested at 2.20 a.m. on 28.10.2006; gave a false name before disclosing true name; no explanation for departure
custody_duration: Not stated (arrest on 28.10.2006 reported; duration of custody not stated)
bail_history: Not stated (appellant was in jail when appealing to Supreme Court)
trial_duration: offence: 27.10.2006; trial judgment: 13.12.2007; High Court: 05.03.2008; Supreme Court: 18.04.2013
legal_representation: Appellant: Pijush K. Roy and Kakali Roy (amicus curiae in the Supreme Court). State: Archana Pathak Dave, Dr. Sumant Bharadwaj, Ankita Chaudhary, Mridula Ray and Milind Kumar
investigation_status: FIR registered (Crime No. 466/2006); post-mortem performed; investigation completed and chargesheet filed; case committed to Sessions Court; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Husband of deceased Seema (Munna) not examined; court held this not fatal to the prosecution case
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302, sentenced to death. High Court: conviction upheld, death commuted to life imprisonment with at least 20 years and no remission. Supreme Court: appeals dismissed
prosecution_argument: Recoveries, extra-judicial confession, false name at arrest, consistent evidence of PWs 1 and 4, and no denial of absconding in s.313 statement established guilt; High Court justified restrictions on remission
defence_argument: No eyewitness; circumstances not satisfactorily established and no complete chain; FIR doubtful; contradictions on where the accused first disclosed the incident; surrounding households not examined; no reliable independent witness; recoveries doubtful; alternatively, remission restriction unjustified
legal_principle_applied: Conviction on circumstantial evidence where absence of eyewitness is not fatal and circumstances must be fully established; extra-judicial confession may be acted upon if voluntary, true and trustworthy; absconding rules out hypothesis of innocence; minimum fixed term without remission after commutation of death sentence
precedent_relied_upon: Shri Bhagwan v. State of Rajasthan (2001) 6 SCC 296; Prakash Dhawal Khairnar v. State of Maharashtra (2002) 2 SCC 35; Ram Anup Singh v. State of Bihar (2002) 6 SCC 686; Nazir Khan v. State of Delhi (2003) 8 SCC 461; Swamy Shraddananda (2) v. State of Karnataka (2008) 13 SCC 767; Haru Ghosh v. State of West Bengal (2009) 15 SCC 551; Ramraj v. State of Chhattisgarh (2010) 1 SCC 573; Neel Kumar v. State of Haryana (2012) 5 SCC 766; Sandeep v. State of UP (2012) 6 SCC 107; Gurvail Singh v. State of Punjab (2013) 2 SCC 713; Jagmohan Singh v. State of UP (1973) 1 SCC 20; Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab (1980) 2 SCC 684. Sangeet v. State of Haryana (2013) 2 SCC 452 held inapplicable
sentencing_rationale: High Court commutation to life with a minimum of 20 years before release and no remission was upheld in view of the five deaths and the line of Supreme Court decisions fixing minimum terms for serious offences after commutation
judicial_aggravating_factors: Five persons died; offence serious in nature
other_sentence_order: High Court direction (affirmed): not to be released until 20 years served including period undergone; no remission by State or Government of India on any occasion
